paragraphs.source_en: Cicadas are forever squirting a stream of urine right at my eyes; if you escape it, well and good, but if you get hit, that is your bad luck. Why must a cicada relieve itself once more just as it is about to fly away? What sort of state of mind, after all, acts upon its physiological mechanism in this way? Can it be from an excess of distress? Or is it a stratagem for flight, meant to take the enemy unawares? If so, it belongs in the same category as the squid spitting ink, the stickleback displaying its poisonous spines, and my master brandishing Latin. This is a question that cicadology cannot afford to neglect; studied thoroughly, it would indeed be worthy as the subject of a doctoral dissertation. But all this is digression; let us return to the main matter. The place where cicadas most like to concentrate, though the word concentrate may sound rather comic, while assemble sounds stale, so concentrate it shall be, is the green paulownia tree. This green paulownia is said to be called wutong in Chinese. But the leaves of this green paulownia grow exceedingly thick, and since each leaf is as large as a round fan, when they crowd together the foliage is so dense that one can hardly see the trunk, which greatly hampers the sport of cicada-catching. It makes me suspect that the popular song about hearing the sweet voice but not seeing the fair form may have been composed especially for me. Having no choice, I simply make my way toward the sound. At a point a little over six feet from the ground the trunk divides neatly into two branches, and there I always take a short rest and reconnoiter the cicadas' whereabouts. Naturally, as I climb up to that spot, the leaves are bound to rustle, and some impatient cicadas fly away. Once a single one takes flight, all is lost; in their talent for imitation, cicadas are no less stupid than human beings. They fly off one after another, and by the time I have struggled up to the fork, I often find the whole tree sunk in silence. Once, after climbing up there, I looked all around every which way and kept twitching my ears, yet could not detect the slightest hint of a cicada. It was too much trouble to start over, so I decided to rest for a while, occupy the fork, and wait for another opportunity. Before long, without realizing it, I grew drowsy and at last went roaming through the sweet black land of dreams. When I woke with a start, I found that I had tumbled from the fork with a thud onto the stone path in the garden. Still, that was only an extreme example of failure; generally speaking, each climb up the tree brings me one or two captures. What takes the pleasure out of it is that, up in the tree, I have to hold the cicada in my mouth. Therefore, whenever I come down from the tree and spit it out, the cicada is usually already dead. No matter how I tease it or scratch at it, there is no definite response at all. The true relish of cicada-catching lies in creeping up quietly on Mr. Cicada and, just as he is frantically stretching and contracting his tail, suddenly pinning him down with my forepaw. At that moment Mr. Cicada lets out a cry of distress and shakes his thin, transparent wings in every direction. The speed of that trembling, the beauty of it, is simply beyond description, truly a grand spectacle in the world of cicadas.

units.source_en: Cicadas are forever squirting a stream of urine right at my eyes; if you escape it, well and good, but if you get hit, that is your bad luck.

ja.t: ってしょぐってくるようだ。

units.source_zh: 蝉动不动就会对准我的眼睛哧地撒上一泡尿，你逃脱了自然好，撒上了算倒霉。

units.source_en: Why must a cicada relieve itself once more just as it is about to fly away?
units.source_zh: 蝉在临飞走时，为什么还要解一次手？

units.source_en: What sort of state of mind, after all, acts upon its physiological mechanism in this way?
units.source_zh: 这究竟是什么样的心理状态作用于生理机能呢？

units.source_en: Can it be from an excess of distress?

ja.t: やはりせつなさのあまりかしらん。

units.source_zh: 是不是也是由于过分难过的缘故呢？

units.source_en: Or is it a stratagem for flight, meant to take the enemy unawares?
units.source_zh: 还是为了出敌不意而采取的逃跑策略呢？

units.source_en: If so, it belongs in the same category as the squid spitting ink, the stickleback displaying its poisonous spines, and my master brandishing Latin.
units.source_zh: 如果是那样的话，这就和乌贼吐墨、刺鱼身带毒刺、我家主人玩弄拉丁语一样了。

units.source_en: This is a question that cicadology cannot afford to neglect; studied thoroughly, it would indeed be worthy as the subject of a doctoral dissertation.

ja.t: すればこれだけでたしかに

units.source_zh: 这是蝉学上不可忽视的问题，如果充分加以研究，确实有做博士论文题目的价值。

units.source_en: But all this is digression; let us return to the main matter.

ja.t: だから、そのくらいにしてまた

units.source_zh: 这些都是闲话，且言归正传吧。

units.source_en: The place where cicadas most like to concentrate, though the word concentrate may sound rather comic, while assemble sounds stale, so concentrate it shall be, is the green paulownia tree.
units.source_zh: 蝉最喜欢集中——使用集中的字眼虽然有些滑稽，但用集合又显得陈腐，所以还是用集中——的地方是青桐树上。

units.source_en: This green paulownia is said to be called wutong in Chinese.
units.source_zh: 青桐树据说在汉语中又称梧桐树。

units.source_en: But the leaves of this green paulownia grow exceedingly thick, and since each leaf is as large as a round fan, when they crowd together the foliage is so dense that one can hardly see the trunk, which greatly hampers the sport of cicada-catching.

ja.t: っている。これがはなはだ

units.source_zh: 不过，这种青桐树的叶子十分茂密，而且叶子有团扇那么大小，这些叶子长在一起，它的茂密程度到了几乎使你看不清树干的地步，这就大有碍于捕蝉运动。

units.source_en: It makes me suspect that the popular song about hearing the sweet voice but not seeing the fair form may have been composed especially for me.

ja.t: しまれるくらいである。

units.source_zh: 它使我怀疑那俗谣中所说“听娇声不见倩影”是不是专为我而作呢。

units.source_en: Having no choice, I simply make my way toward the sound.
units.source_zh: 我无奈只好向有叫声的地方走去。

units.source_en: At a point a little over six feet from the ground the trunk divides neatly into two branches, and there I always take a short rest and reconnoiter the cicadas' whereabouts.

ja.t: になっているから、ここで

units.source_zh: 从地面往上六尺多高的地方树干正好分成两叉，我总是在这里稍事休息，侦察一下蝉所呆的地方。

units.source_en: Naturally, as I climb up to that spot, the leaves are bound to rustle, and some impatient cicadas fly away.
units.source_zh: 当然，在我爬往这个地方时，树叶子难免发生簌簌的声响，有些急性子的蝉便飞走了。

units.source_en: Once a single one takes flight, all is lost; in their talent for imitation, cicadas are no less stupid than human beings.
units.source_zh: 只要有一只飞起来，那就糟啦，在跟着学样儿这点上，蝉的愚蠢并不比人差。

units.source_en: They fly off one after another, and by the time I have struggled up to the fork, I often find the whole tree sunk in silence.
units.source_zh: 它们接二连三都飞了起来，等我费力地爬到树杈的地方，经常是满树寂然无声的场面。

units.source_en: Once, after climbing up there, I looked all around every which way and kept twitching my ears, yet could not detect the slightest hint of a cicada.
units.source_zh: 曾经有过一次，我爬到树上，不管怎样四面环顾，不断摆动我的耳朵，丝毫也感觉不出有蝉。

units.source_en: It was too much trouble to start over, so I decided to rest for a while, occupy the fork, and wait for another opportunity.
units.source_zh: 重新再来太麻烦了，于是我决定暂时休息一下，据守在树杈上等待新的机会。

units.source_en: Before long, without realizing it, I grew drowsy and at last went roaming through the sweet black land of dreams.
units.source_zh: 没多久，我不知不觉困倦起来，终于进入黑色的甜蜜梦乡畅游起来。

units.source_en: When I woke with a start, I found that I had tumbled from the fork with a thud onto the stone path in the garden.
units.source_zh: 当我猛地惊醒，不料从树杈上咚的一声掉到了院子里铺着石子的路面上了。

units.source_en: Still, that was only an extreme example of failure; generally speaking, each climb up the tree brings me one or two captures.
units.source_zh: 不过，这只是极端失败的例子，一般地讲，每爬一次树总可以捉到一两只的。

units.source_en: What takes the pleasure out of it is that, up in the tree, I have to hold the cicada in my mouth.

ja.t: えてしまわなくてはならん。

units.source_zh: 使我索然无趣的是，我在树上就得把它衔在嘴里。

units.source_en: Therefore, whenever I come down from the tree and spit it out, the cicada is usually already dead.
units.source_zh: 因此，每当我从树上下来，再把蝉吐出的时候，一般蝉已经死了。

units.source_en: No matter how I tease it or scratch at it, there is no definite response at all.
units.source_zh: 任凭我怎样逗弄它，怎样挠它，都已毫无反应。

units.source_en: The true relish of cicada-catching lies in creeping up quietly on Mr. Cicada and, just as he is frantically stretching and contracting his tail, suddenly pinning him down with my forepaw.

ja.t: ましたりしているところを、わっと

units.source_zh: 捕蝉的真正妙味在于我悄悄地靠近寒蝉君，瞄准它正在拼命把尾巴一伸一缩的当儿，用我的前脚猛地把它按住的时候。

units.source_en: At that moment Mr. Cicada lets out a cry of distress and shakes his thin, transparent wings in every direction.
units.source_zh: 这时，寒蝉君就会发出哀鸣，前后左右地抖动着它那薄而透明的翅膀。

units.source_en: The speed of that trembling, the beauty of it, is simply beyond description, truly a grand spectacle in the world of cicadas.
units.source_zh: 它抖得那个快呀、那个美呀，简直是无法形容，真是蝉世界的一大奇观！

paragraphs.source_zh: 蝉动不动就会对准我的眼睛哧地撒上一泡尿，你逃脱了自然好，撒上了算倒霉。蝉在临飞走时，为什么还要解一次手？这究竟是什么样的心理状态作用于生理机能呢？是不是也是由于过分难过的缘故呢？还是为了出敌不意而采取的逃跑策略呢？如果是那样的话，这就和乌贼吐墨、刺鱼身带毒刺、我家主人玩弄拉丁语一样了。这是蝉学上不可忽视的问题，如果充分加以研究，确实有做博士论文题目的价值。这些都是闲话，且言归正传吧。蝉最喜欢集中——使用集中的字眼虽然有些滑稽，但用集合又显得陈腐，所以还是用集中——的地方是青桐树上。青桐树据说在汉语中又称梧桐树。不过，这种青桐树的叶子十分茂密，而且叶子有团扇那么大小，这些叶子长在一起，它的茂密程度到了几乎使你看不清树干的地步，这就大有碍于捕蝉运动。它使我怀疑那俗谣中所说“听娇声不见倩影”是不是专为我而作呢。我无奈只好向有叫声的地方走去。从地面往上六尺多高的地方树干正好分成两叉，我总是在这里稍事休息，侦察一下蝉所呆的地方。当然，在我爬往这个地方时，树叶子难免发生簌簌的声响，有些急性子的蝉便飞走了。只要有一只飞起来，那就糟啦，在跟着学样儿这点上，蝉的愚蠢并不比人差。它们接二连三都飞了起来，等我费力地爬到树杈的地方，经常是满树寂然无声的场面。曾经有过一次，我爬到树上，不管怎样四面环顾，不断摆动我的耳朵，丝毫也感觉不出有蝉。重新再来太麻烦了，于是我决定暂时休息一下，据守在树杈上等待新的机会。没多久，我不知不觉困倦起来，终于进入黑色的甜蜜梦乡畅游起来。当我猛地惊醒，不料从树杈上咚的一声掉到了院子里铺着石子的路面上了。不过，这只是极端失败的例子，一般地讲，每爬一次树总可以捉到一两只的。使我索然无趣的是，我在树上就得把它衔在嘴里。因此，每当我从树上下来，再把蝉吐出的时候，一般蝉已经死了。任凭我怎样逗弄它，怎样挠它，都已毫无反应。捕蝉的真正妙味在于我悄悄地靠近寒蝉君，瞄准它正在拼命把尾巴一伸一缩的当儿，用我的前脚猛地把它按住的时候。这时，寒蝉君就会发出哀鸣，前后左右地抖动着它那薄而透明的翅膀。它抖得那个快呀、那个美呀，简直是无法形容，真是蝉世界的一大奇观！

paragraphs.source_en: Whenever I pin down Mr. Cicada, I always ask him to show me this artistic performance. When I have watched enough, I make no ceremony about stuffing him into my mouth and swallowing him down in a few bites. Some cicadas even continue this artistic performance after they have entered my mouth.

units.source_en: Whenever I pin down Mr. Cicada, I always ask him to show me this artistic performance.
units.source_zh: 我每次按住寒蝉君时，总是请它给我来一番这种艺术性的表演。

units.source_en: When I have watched enough, I make no ceremony about stuffing him into my mouth and swallowing him down in a few bites.

ja.t: それがいやになるとご

units.source_zh: 等我观赏够了，便不客气地把它叼在嘴里，三下两下咽下去了。

units.source_en: Some cicadas even continue this artistic performance after they have entered my mouth.

ja.t: をつづけているのがある。

units.source_zh: 也有的蝉，甚至进入我的嘴里，还要继续这种艺术表演哩。

paragraphs.source_zh: 我每次按住寒蝉君时，总是请它给我来一番这种艺术性的表演。等我观赏够了，便不客气地把它叼在嘴里，三下两下咽下去了。也有的蝉，甚至进入我的嘴里，还要继续这种艺术表演哩。
